title: Sparky and the Singing Puddle
markdown:
There was a wizard named Cedric. He lived in a cozy cottage tucked in the deep valleys of Hazelhowe. Chimney smoke curled like playful ribbons. His garden burst with flowers that seemed to giggle in the breeze. His special friend was Sparky, a proud dragonet with scales the colour of emeralds that almost winked. Sparky always puffed out his chest, trying to look grand, even when he was just chasing butterflies.

One sunny afternoon, the perfect kind for an adventure, Cedric packed a picnic: plump jam tarts still warm, crusty cheese sandwiches cut into triangles, a gleaming flask of fizzy elderflower cordial that tickled the nose. He set the basket by the door, wicker handle peeking out. When he turned back for his favourite striped scarf, the basket was gone. Vanished.

“Oh dear. Sparky, my picnic basket. Have you seen it?”

Sparky had been admiring his reflection in a big dewdrop on a daisy. A little puff of smoke that smelled like toast. “Perhaps it grew legs and walked away. Or a mischievous pixie borrowed it for a game.”

Cedric sighed like a gentle breeze. “That’s not very helpful. Pixies are too busy polishing their wings. We must find it.” Tall pointed hat with a little crescent moon. Trusty wand. He was not sure what magic would find a lost picnic basket, but he hoped for the best.

They set off toward the woods. Fresh air, pine needles, damp soil kissed by a sprinkle of rain. The path led to a very big inviting puddle that shimmered like a fallen piece of sky, reflecting fluffy clouds. Here was Sparky’s curious quirk: he absolutely, completely, firmly refused to cross puddles. Unless, of course, you sang to them. And Cedric, flustered and forgetful when jam tarts were at stake, had not packed his singing book.

“Oh, bother and bewilderment. We can’t get across. Not without a song.”

Sparky puffed out his chest. “Puddles are to be admired from a safe and dry distance. They splash. They are alarmingly wet.” He shivered, though the day was warm.

A knot of worry, tangled yarn. Jam tarts, cheese sandwiches, fizzy cordial—all in that basket. He imagined them soggy and stale. “We have to get across. It’s important for our picnic adventure. Just a little hop? We can pretend it’s a magic carpet ride.”

Sparky stayed put, emerald eyes wide. “A song. Or a story about a brave knight who didn’t get his boots wet. Or about a dragon who flew over it.”

Cedric wrung his hands. Good at making flowers bloom and finding lost socks. Not good at making up songs or dragon tales on the spot. “Alright. I’ll go ahead. You stay here and guard this spot. I’ll be back with the basket.”

He stepped toward the dark edge of the woods. Sparky watched, a flicker of worry, a tiny puff of smoke like a sigh of mist. Then, with a very careful one-pawed step, he slowly followed Cedric into the trees.

Just as Cedric began to wonder if he would ever taste a jam tart again, a tiny voice chirped from the shade of a fern. “Lost something, have we? You look a bit basket-less.”

Perched on a green frond: a dragonet even smaller than Sparky, scales shimmering with all the colours of a rainbow. Glint.

“Indeed. My picnic basket. And Sparky won’t cross puddles unless I sing to them, and I don’t have a song ready.”

Glint giggled like tiny silver bells. “Oh, Sparky. He’s a proud one. But I quite like singing. Especially songs about wonderful things puddles can be.”

He fluttered to the edge of the big puddle, puffed out his chest, and sang, voice clear and surprisingly loud:

“Oh, puddle, puddle, shiny and wide,
Don’t you dare splash when we step inside!
You’re just a mirror for the sky so blue,
A little pathway for me and you!
A watery dance floor, a silvery gleam,
A tiny reflection of a happy dream!”

Sparky, peeking from the other side, perked up his ears. The song was good. Glint’s voice like a brook. The puddle as a mirror seemed less scary. A tentative step. Then another. To Cedric’s delight, Sparky splashed right through. Not a single drop hit his precious scales.

They ventured deeper. Trees denser, path muddier, spirits high. A strong gust sent leaves dancing like playful confetti. Then a rustle in the bushes. Rustle, rustle, crunch. Cedric’s heart thumped. He imagined a grumpy troll.

It was only a fluffy-tailed rabbit. It hopped out, twitched its nose, sniffed them, and bounded away. Glint laughed. “Just a bunny. Not quite as fearsome as a puddle.”

Sparky huffed smoke, scales gleaming with relief.

Soon the cheerful gurgle of a stream. Tucked beside a large mossy stone: Cedric’s picnic basket, perfectly safe, not a jam tart out of place. The familiar scent of cheese and sweet jam. He let out a long breath.

They found a soft grassy spot by the stream and spread a colourful blanket. Fizzy elderflower tasted extra special. Sparky did not mind the damp grass when cheese sandwiches were passed his way. Glint told stories of the sky and the wind. Cedric watched Sparky and Glint chase a sunbeam. The tarts were still warm. The puddle, behind them, went on being a mirror.
characters: Cedric (young wizard who packs picnics), Sparky (a proud dragonet who will not cross puddles)
author: StoryGen Community
